# Faultline

> Faultline is the operational improvement system for production lines, by Opex Elevate. It covers the whole improvement lifecycle — identifying opportunities, diagnosing problems, applying a methodology, organising delivery and verifying results — with every finding said in money, measured by people and worked out by formula. Offline-first, installable on the phones and laptops a team already has.

Faultline is made by Opex Elevate (UK). It is invite-only — there is no public sign-up. Domain: faultline.opexelevate.co.uk.

## The lifecycle

- **Identify the opportunity.** Time the stops, count the losses, walk the line — the biggest losses in minutes, packs and pounds, line by line across the factory.
- **Diagnose the problem.** Capability, reliability, line capacity and balance, losses, analysis and root cause: the technical tools, each measured by people and worked out by formula.
- **Apply a methodology.** A project is one of eight methods — PDCA, DMAIC, 8D, A3, Stage gate, Kaizen event, Improvement Kata, Theory of Constraints — each with its sections in order and the tools that fit each section.
- **Organise the delivery.** Projects, actions with who owes what by when, programs and tests proved on the line, the journey day by day.
- **Verify the result.** A measured before and after on the same number, every finding in money, and the papers to hand over.

## What it is not

- Not a project-management system: a project is the delivery part of the lifecycle, no more.
- Not a sensor or OEE system: people record what they see.
- No sensors, no integrations, no IT project.

## Key pages

- [Home / the app](https://faultline.opexelevate.co.uk/): sign-in.
- [How it works — real screens](https://faultline.opexelevate.co.uk/how-it-works.html): screen by screen.

## Facts

- Audience: operations, engineering and continuous-improvement leads in manufacturing, in particular food and other fast-moving consumer goods.
- Platform: installable web app (PWA), offline-first, background sync; phones, tablets, laptops.
- Access: invite-only; a project's owner adds people by email.
